Google Trekker

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
We all know about the wonders of Google street view and would have possibly have seen Google street cars buzzing around but now Google have come up with Google trekker. The idea is to film off road wilderness areas like the Grand Canyon and the Amazon –wilderness spots only accessible on foot. The Google Trekker program is giving people the kit to map their area of the world with the idea of making the world accessible and to encourage people to get out and enjoy the environment. Andre Van Kets and enthusiastic travel geek has been given a Google trekker to map South Africa’s wilderness areas over the next 6 months. He and his team will walk the 22 Nature Reserves and 8 Unesco heritage sites with the aim to promote the natural beauty of South Africa. Not only will people be able to explore these places from the safety of their couches but it will help them choose which travel destination they want to explore. It's a story about innovative technology and how it is enhancing our lives

Further information:
The Google Trekker camera looks a bit like a walking spootnik. It’s strapped to one’s back- it only works out doors as it has to connect to satellite and films every 2 seconds with the help of 15 cameras –shooting in all directions. There is a computer capturing the images and everything is controlled via Bluetooth on your phone. This footage is then stitched together to give a panoramic view.
The team consist of a trekker carrying the 22 kg Google trekker camera gear and a videography armed with cameras and drones to film the “trekker” doing it’s thing. The idea is also to feature different characters on different routes like local hikers, mountain rescuers, game rangers and interesting characters showing you their favorite places and routes. Ultimately it will showcase routes and views and the people and their passion for them.
This is the first Google Trek in Africa and the footage will stand alongside the Treks of the Mont Blanch, the Sahara desert, antartic, etc etc as Google begins to document the world.
Andre and his crew have already started hiking around Table Mountain following the paths from the front Table over to Cape Point. Every week they fill a drive with footage and ship it off to Switzerland to be stitched together. Once it’s done there will be a launch of routes around South Africa. The idea would be to accompany them on one of their hikes around the Western Cape and feature some of the routes and people as well as explore the technology

Press Release:


Google Trekker
Intrepid explorers hauling a 22 kilogram Google Trekker camera on their backs capture the spectacular natural beauty of local wilderness areas like never before. Carte Blanche heads off the beaten track.


Script:


Script: We have all used Google street view to check out a location or get directions but what about the off road places?
Link: Google trekker takes street view to an entirely new level as Google tries to develop a comprehensive map of the entire world, this is the interface between technology and the wilderness
Script: Andre van Kets travel agent and self-confessed geek was researching how to expose South Africa’s natural wilderness and heritage online, and came across Google trekker
Andre “When I saw this device the dots just joined for me and I knew we had to get South Africa’s prime tourist attractions online so that they could be virtually experienced to inspire more travellers to actually come out here and see all this beauty
Script: When he discovered the trekker was available to be loaned by anyone in the world who wished to show off their neck of the woods, he immediately applied
Andre “It’s a crowd source program that basically Google is looking for people all over the world to do this. The Grand Canyon has been trekked, out the pyramids of geyser have been trekked out they have put this thing on camels through the Sahara desert. This is a program where people from all corners of the world are contributing to something for everyone in the world. This is the now the first time they are doing Africa and they are starting here in South Africa it’s quite exciting
Script: To his surprise Google responded, 4 months later the kit arrived and Trek South Africa got going. Grant Clark a close friend got roped in and has spent the last two months trekking the wilderness areas around Cape Town
John “You say that Google were confronted by how to get out of the car and their answer was to strap 22 kgs of equipment to somebodies back
Grant “We ask this question daily why does this thing weigh 22 kgs. You know I have done a few hikes on my own and I think you have to be physically fit to be able to pick that thing up, put it onto your back and then walk 10-15 ks for the day so it’s not easy and it can be quite tough”
John “What have been the most dangerous parts for you?
Grant “Skeleton gorge near Kirstenbosch Gardens, it’s like being on a step machine for 3 hours with 22 kgs on your back and we did it a few days after the rains had come so a lot of waterfalls lots of water very slippery ja a few skety moments . I think you do have to be constantly aware of where you are putting your foot, and where the edge is the fact that you don’t want to lean back or forward too much to look at the view because you might just fall into it. You got to be quite an experienced hiker, you just have to be constantly be aware of what’s on your back
Script: And is a bit like being the pied piper gathering people along the way. This bizarre contraption has prompted some interesting questions- is it cell phone mast, a robot or a 3D ejector seat. Fellow mountain enthusiast Jody Summers came across them while out hiking with his group
Jody “Right on top of Skeleton Gorge I came across this guy carrying this huge thing on his back appearing out of the mist and I was like what has he got on his back. And I guess Andre could see the excitement on my face and then he invited me to come on a co-trek with him and the rest of the Google trekkers. After my first time I was hooked. I love it I mean I can tell my kids one day go on Google Maps and check out this trail and yup your dad did that one it’s pretty awesome and I am quite excited about this project and being a part of the family and the team it’s amazing
Grant “ So you want to be 15 to 20 meters away from each other, try not to get people in the shot, if someone walks past you that’s’ fine they are probably going to freek out and ask you questions but try just keep walking forwards at a steady pace and tell to ask them to ask the person behind you all about what you are wearing. At the moment it is just talking to the Bluetooth connector so you don’t need wireless you don’t need signal its just the Google trekker and your phone
Script: The cameras record every two seconds and store the data on hard drives on the backpack. A modem connects them via satellite to head office in Switzerland so they can keep track of all the trekkers out on the loan program and give them feedback if there is a leaf on the lens or the cameras have misted up.
Grant “At the end of each day we have to write up a report so we have to tell Google where we have been what were the interesting parts of it were they anything funny or dangerous happen. Just set down the coordinates of where we have been and at the end of each week once the hard drives are full we send them off to Google
Script: Ntsiki Daki relatively new to walking on Table Mountain started a hiking club encouraging black youth to venture into new places.
Daki “The idea is to get a lot more black people to come up hiking and basically explore the city and see the beautiful views of Cape Town. We can share the spaces, have the conversations, just to break the stereotype and get people to talk to each other.
Script: Excited by the technology Ntsiki joined Trek South Africa to help map the routes and looks forward to using them for his group
Daki “Right now we have to look at routes ourselves the organising team before we bring anyone else so it’s going to make it a lot more easier for us to explore even before we go to that place so we are able to know if it is a difficult hike is it easy how long does it take basically just to see it and share with other people for them to know if they want to join us for that specific hike
Andre “The primary use is for people who have never been to SA to get a sense of it in the most immersive way possible with a click of a button you can drop yourself into a 360 world that’s 1000’s of miles away.
“When you are on google maps …so we are going to look at Table Mountain..and if you click on the little pegman at the bottom as Google has called him…and you can see there is a whole bunch of roads here which the street view cars cover and over here we have a sort of jaggered line and that’s a trail that the google trekker has explored. So right now we have been transported to the top of Table mountain and you can see Lions Head in the distance and I can pan around 360 so this what we are looking at right now is one of the photos we took on the trail today or the equivalent where that camera with 15 pointing in all directions , is capturing this scene and all you have to do is and all you have to do is click a little further down the trail
John “I understand that you would described t as being stitched together
Andre “ Correct, so first all 15 cameras are woven into one 360 sphere and then all of those sphere are connected one to another along the trails
John “And the stand out for me is that you can see incredible detail this blade of grass for instance you can see Lions Head in the distance you can see Robben Island in the distance so the clarity is extraordinary”
Links: “Google trekker has been on the go for 3 years now and people are taking to Wildernesses across the globe and with views like this it’s easy to understand why the same is happening here
Andre “We have got 6 months ahead where we are hoping to cover all the national parks is SA there are 8 world UNESCO world heritage sites which we have got on our hit list, so we want to take this everywhere and anywhere and we want to meet all the people in SA that are passionate about their neck of the woods.

This is the first Google Trek in Africa and the footage will stand alongside the Treks of the Mont Blanch, the Sahara desert, antartic, etc etc as Google begins to document the world. Andre and his crew have already started hiking around Table Mountain following the paths from the front Table over to Cape Point. Every week they fill a drive with footage and ship it off to Switzerland to be stitched together. Once it’s done there will be a launch of routes around South Africa. The idea would be to accompany them on one of their hikes around the Western Cape and feature some of the routes and people as well as explore the technology
